data.name: Horace
data.gender_notes: Horace is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman family name Horatius, which is derived from the Roman god Saturn, who was believed to be the god of agriculture, time, and wealth. The name Horace could also mean 'one who hides'. In the Christian tradition, it is associated with Saint Horace, a martyr in the Roman Empire. The name Horace carries the meaning “Time keeper, one who hides” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Horace usually hope their child will grow to embody time keeper, one who hides and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the idea of hiding one's faith in times of persecution.
data.etymology: Horace belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Time keeper, one who hides.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Horace total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: הוראס
in_hebrew.meaning: חורס הוא שם שפירושו זמן, עונה או שעה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: הוראס הוא שם שמקורו בשפה הרומית, אך אין לו שורשים עבריים ישירים. עם זאת, ניתן לראות כיורש או הורוס, שם שפירושו 'זמן' או 'עונה', וקשור למושגים של תזמון אלוהי ושעון הקוסמוס. בהקשר נוצרי, השם עשוי לסמל את מושג הזמן האלוהי ורצון האל.

in_greek.name: Χοράτιος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χοράτιος προέρχεται από τη Ρώμη και συγκεκριμένα από το λατινικό όνομα Horatius. Στην ελληνική παράδοση, το όνομα αυτό δεν έχει άμεση αναφορά, αλλά μπορεί να συνδεθεί με λέξεις που σημαίνουν 'ώρα' ή 'στιγμή'. Στην πνευματική και πολιτιστική παράδοση της Ανατολικής Ορθοδοξίας, το όνομα μπορεί να αντιπροσωπεύει τη σημασία του χρόνου και της στιγμής στην πνευματική πορεία.

The name Horace has been used in various Christian cultures to signify awareness of temporal and spiritual realities.

in_english.name: Horace
in_english.long_meaning: The name Horace comes from the Latin 'Horatius', which is associated with 'hora', meaning 'hour' or 'season'. While not directly mentioned in the Bible, the concept of time and seasons is crucial in Christian theology. Horace symbolizes an awareness of temporal moments and their spiritual significance. Historically, the name has been used across Christian cultures to reflect on the fleeting nature of time and the importance of making each moment count spiritually.

data.cultural_impact: The name Horace has its origins rooted in ancient Roman culture. Named after the Roman god Saturn, Horace underscores a connection to nature and agriculture, reflecting the values of the Roman civilization. The name also signifies the idea of 'hiding,' which may be interpreted as 'protection,' 'secrecy,' or 'concealment,' which has shaped its use as a personal name throughout history.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian context, the name Horace takes on a deeper meaning as a reminder of the preciousness of our faith, which can be seen as a hidden treasure. Similar to the symbolism of the Roman god Saturn, Horace signifies the abundance, protection, and wisdom that come with embracing a spiritual life. Furthermore, Saint Horace, a 3rd-century martyr and bishop, exemplifies the faith and courage required to live according to one's beliefs. This name can serve as a daily reminder of the hidden but transformative power of faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Horace, meaning "having a strong or stern aspect," in Latin, symbolizes strength and determination in one's faith journey. This name may inspire the bearer to face challenges with unwavering resolve and courage, embodying the spirit of resilience and endurance in the Christian walk.
